newsitem.title: UK: BTPs take the lead in weekly bond index -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: BTPs take the lead in weekly bond index -Salomon.

text.p: Italian BTPs led the field in a week of relatively modest performance by government bond markets, Salomon Brothers said on Friday. Overall the Salomon Brothers world government bond index gained 0.08 percent in the week to Thursday.

Markets have been rife with speculation about European interest rates the past few days and on Tuesday the Bank of Italy cut its key discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.50 percent, the lowest level for over 20 years.
BTPs made gains of 0.43 percent in lire, closely followed by British gilts which notched up 0.40 percent in sterling.
Within core Europe, French bonds gained 0.18 percent to take sixth place in the index but German Bunds, at thirteenth, made a loss of 0.07 percent in local currency terms.
Japanese government bonds too made losses to the tune of 0.13 percent but Swedish bonds showed the greatest deficit, losing investors 0.44 percent.

In dollar terms only U.S. Treasuries made gains, proffering 0.13 percent. The other 15 government bonds in the index showed U.S. dollar losses of between 0.03 percent, for Canadian bonds, and 4.72 percent for Swedish bonds.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
